svg.title: Breadboard layout for the ESP32-S3 phygital sensor hub
svg.desc: Two half-size breadboards joined with their power rails removed. The ESP32-S3 straddles the seam. A 5V battery powers the rails; the S3 runs from USB. Radars and mic connect with jumpers on the left board; the amp, RGB LED and resistors plug into the right board.
svg.text: One 220 Ω resistor per colour, between the GPIO
and that colour's leg. Never on the common leg.
On the board: each resistor jumps the channel,
from the pin's row (column e) to the same row
LED legs go in column h, rows 7–10: R, K, G, B.
A black jumper takes K (row 8) to the GND rail.
*Leg order varies by maker; check your LED's sheet.
Not to scale. Push the S3 in across the seam wherever its pins fit; what matters is the row each wire goes in.
Every hole in a half-row (a–e or f–j) is connected, so any free hole in a pin's half-row works.
